decisions.executionNote: Approach the yellow nut with the right arm, raising and pitching the wrist gradually; preserve elbow-up continuity and inspect before descent.
Finish vertical tool orientation and center above the yellow nut; descend only to a pregrasp height for visual alignment.
Lower around the yellow nut and close gently; grasp retention is not yet established.
Lift the yellow nut and carry it above the matching yellow screw, keeping the gripper closed and the tool vertical.
The yellow nut is retained. Lower coaxially onto the yellow screw, with a small lateral correction from the wrist view.
Begin clockwise tightening of the yellow nut while maintaining axial alignment and a small downward feed.
Yellow engagement is uncertain from the hole view. Make a small lateral alignment correction and a short additional clockwise turn before regripping.
Release and raise slightly to inspect the yellow alignment, while resetting the wrist for another tightening grip.
The released yellow nut is visibly tilted, not complete. Clear the right gripper and begin a controlled left-arm approach to the upright purple nut.
Move the left wrist toward the central purple nut at clearance height, completing the downward approach orientation without crossing the arms.
Center the left gripper over the upright purple nut and descend to pregrasp height. The right arm remains clear of the central workspace.
Lower and close around the purple nut, then lift slightly to verify retention visually; use a small centering correction.
Corrected the rejected tensor; no prior motion occurred. Lift the retained purple nut and carry it over its matching screw while keeping both workspaces separated.
Use the wrist view to reduce the purple nut's lateral offset from the screw axis, then descend slowly toward engagement without twisting yet.
Refine purple alignment using the observed screw-axis displacement. Make a smaller reverse lateral correction and a gentle axial seating motion.
The purple screw tip is now visible inside the nut. Apply a controlled clockwise tightening stroke with a small axial feed and maintain the closed grasp.
Purple remains coaxial with the screw. Open the fingers and reset the wrist without reversing the nut, preparing another tightening stroke.
Regrip the purple nut and apply a second clockwise stroke with a small axial feed; monitor the screw tip and nut orientation for continued engagement.
Reset the open left wrist for another purple tightening stroke. In the separate right workspace, approach the displaced yellow nut from above for recovery.
Apply a third purple tightening stroke while lowering and resetting the open right wrist around the recovered yellow nut.
Reset the left wrist with fingers open. Recenter and grasp the upright yellow nut with the right hand, then lift for a retention check.
Apply a fourth purple tightening stroke. Lift the recovered yellow nut clear of its screw and translate above the matching shaft for careful realignment.
Reset the open left wrist again. Center the yellow nut on the visible shaft and lower slowly toward engagement, without twisting until seating is visible.
Both screw tips are visibly inside their matching nuts. Apply a fifth purple stroke and the first recovered-yellow clockwise stroke, with small axial feeds and closed grippers.
Release and lift clear of the purple pair to inspect its upright retention. Reset the open right wrist for another yellow tightening stroke.
Purple remains upright after release. Park the left arm clear and reset its wrist, while applying a second recovered-yellow tightening stroke.
The yellow screw tip is nearly flush with the nut. Release and lift clear, then approach the remaining blue nut in the right workspace with an open gripper.
Yellow remains upright after release. Center the right wrist above the blue nut and lower to a pregrasp height, leaving the left arm clear.
Use the blue nut's wrist-view offset to refine lateral centering while descending slowly with the gripper open.
Finish blue-nut centering along the wrist viewing direction, close at grasp height, and lift slightly to check retention before the central transfer.
Blue retention is visible. Raise the nut and begin carrying it toward a central tabletop transfer location, keeping the left arm parked clear.
Continue the retained blue nut toward the center at clearance height; stop on the right side of the midline for a tabletop transfer rather than crossing arms.
Lower the blue nut to the central tabletop and release it upright. Keep the left arm stationary until the right gripper has cleared the transfer area.
Blue is released upright in the center. Raise and withdraw the open right gripper into its own workspace before the left arm approaches.
Approach the central blue nut with the left arm after the right arm has cleared. Preserve clearance above the completed purple pair, then descend toward pregrasp.
Descend vertically around the central blue nut with the left gripper open, pausing just above grasp height to verify centering.
Correct the small blue-nut offset in the left wrist view, close at grasp height, and lift a little to verify the tabletop transfer succeeded.
Blue is retained by the left gripper. Lift above the assembled purple pair and carry the nut over the remaining blue screw without crossing the arms.
Lower the blue nut toward the screw with a small lateral correction from the wrist view. Pause before tightening to verify the tip enters the hole.
The blue screw tip is entering the nut but slightly off-center. Make a small reverse lateral correction, seat gently, and begin a short clockwise stroke.
Blue engagement is not yet secure. Relieve contact slightly and realign the nut toward the shaft using both views, without further twisting until the tip is centered.
The blue shaft is laterally centered but still appears above the nut opening in the wrist projection. Seat the nut slowly downward without rotation and inspect for actual entry.
The blue nut has visibly tilted during seating, so stop tightening. Release it and lift the left gripper clear to inspect and recover an upright grasp.
The blue nut has settled upright beside its screw. Reset the left wrist and approach the nut's new visible position for a centered recovery grasp.
Descend toward the recovered blue nut with a small lateral centering correction; keep the fingers open until its position at grasp height is verified.
Close around the upright blue nut at the revised grasp position and lift vertically to verify retention before attempting screw alignment again.
The recovered blue nut is held upright. Raise above the shaft and translate over it slowly, preserving the new centered grasp for a fresh insertion attempt.
The blue shaft is laterally centered in the wrist view after regrasp. Lower vertically without twisting or lateral corrections, then inspect whether the tip enters the nut.
The blue screw tip now appears inside the centered nut. Apply a controlled clockwise stroke with a small downward feed, keeping the grasp closed.
Reset the open left wrist to inspect blue engagement and prepare another stroke. Begin returning the clear right arm toward its home posture with small continuous increments.
Correct the rejected tensor from the unchanged observation. Tighten the engaged blue nut and continue the right arm toward its home pose.
Reset the open left wrist for a further blue tightening stroke without unwinding the nut. Settle the right arm at its home pose.
Regrip the upright blue nut and apply another clockwise tightening stroke with a small axial feed; the right arm stays open at home.
The blue tip is close to flush and the nut remains upright. Reset the open left wrist for one short finishing stroke, keeping the right arm at home.
Apply the final controlled blue tightening stroke with a modest axial feed, maintaining the closed grasp and upright alignment.
Release the blue nut and lift clear while resetting the left wrist. Inspect all three pairs after release before completing the return to origin.
All three pairs remain upright after release. Return the open left arm toward home along a continuous elbow-up path while keeping the right arm at home.
Complete the left arm's return to origin with both grippers open. Keep the assembled pairs untouched and allow tracking to settle at home.
Settle both open grippers at their original poses and observe the released pairs without disturbing them.
Both arms are at origin with grippers open. Hold clear and observe that the three assembled pairs remain stable.
The purple screw tip appears more recessed than the other two. Reapproach with the left arm for a close depth check and, if needed, a controlled finishing turn.
Center the open left gripper above the purple pair and finish the vertical approach orientation, leaving clearance for a close alignment check.
The purple tip remains recessed. Lower and regrip the upright nut with a small centering adjustment for a finishing turn, keeping the other pairs undisturbed.
Apply a controlled clockwise finishing stroke to the centered purple nut with a small axial feed, monitoring the visible screw tip for increased depth.
Purple remains upright but its tip is still recessed. Open and reset the left wrist without reversing the nut, preparing a further controlled tightening stroke.
Regrip the purple nut and advance it with another controlled clockwise stroke and a small downward feed; the blue and yellow pairs remain untouched.
Reset the open left wrist without unwinding the purple nut. Its screw tip remains recessed, so inspect the seating before the next finishing stroke.
Regrip and advance the purple nut through another controlled clockwise stroke with a small downward feed, keeping the other two pairs undisturbed.
Release the purple nut and lift clear to inspect its settled alignment and depth. Reset the open wrist above the pair rather than continuing to load it.
Purple remains upright after the finishing strokes and release. Withdraw the open left arm toward origin, preserving elbow-up continuity and leaving all three pairs untouched.
Complete the left arm's return to origin with both grippers open, leaving the three released matching pairs undisturbed.
Settle both arms at their original poses with grippers fully open and observe the three released assemblies without disturbing them.
Hold both arms clear at origin and leave the released matching assemblies stable; completion depth remains judged from the camera views.
Maintain both open grippers at origin, clear of the three stable matching assemblies.
Keep both arms at origin with grippers open and leave the three released assemblies undisturbed.
Maintain both open grippers at origin, clear of the stable matching assemblies.
